body:
A Le Bail fit with the cell, profile and instrument at the **true** values and only the background free ends at Rwp 1.62 % on a synthetic pattern, and stays there from 100 to 400 `lebail_cycles`. The Rietveld fit of the true structure (intensities not free) reaches 1.09 % and a Pawley fit of the same reflections (intensities free, least squares) 1.06 %. Intensities that are free should not fit worse than the structure they are free to reproduce.

## Expected, and the source

Le Bail's intensities are unconstrained (`docs/manual/using/refining.md`, the `Stage.lebail_cycles` paragraph: the number of intensity-partitioning refreshes), so a Le Bail fit has the freedom of the Rietveld fit and more, and the Rwp ordering Le Bail ≤ Rietveld is what the method is read for (`lebail_gap` in the report compares them). I do not claim the EM partition is a least-squares optimiser, so it may stop above the Pawley minimum; I report how far above, and where.

## Actual (`main` 65a78ab7, numpy + rietx only)

```
Rietveld from the true structure, background free:                     0.0109
Le Bail, cell and profile at the truth, background free, lebail_cycles=3:   0.0456
Le Bail, ... lebail_cycles=100:                                        0.0163
Le Bail, ... lebail_cycles=400:                                        0.0162
Pawley, the same:                                                      0.0106
```

The deficit sits at high angle. Normalised residual (y − calc)/√y, rms per 10° of 2θ, Le Bail at 400 cycles against the true model: 60–90°: 1.03–1.06 against 1.02–1.11; 90–150°: 1.4–2.8 against 1.0–1.1, with the mean signed residual +0.5 to +0.9 there (calc low). Below 60° the two agree to 0.05. Pawley, with the same background and profile, removes it, so the profile and the background are not the cause; the partition's fixed point is.

Run on the pattern's own passes (`plan="profile_only"`, 4 passes, seeded background) the Le Bail Rwp is 1.72, 1.81, 1.82, 1.82 %: it rises from pass to pass, the "Le Bail sits above Rietveld" a benchmark run saw on a CW-neutron set.

<details><summary>the runnable repro</summary>

```python
import numpy as np, rietx as rx
P = rx.Parameter
def phase():
    cell = rx.Cell(a=P(value=5.74), b=P(value=7.69), c=P(value=5.54), alpha=P(value=90.), beta=P(value=90.), gamma=P(value=90.))
    at = lambda l, s, x, y, z, b: rx.Atom(label=l, species=s, x=P(value=x), y=P(value=y), z=P(value=z), biso=P(value=b))
    return rx.Phase(name="pv", space_group="P n m a", cell=cell, scale=P(value=1.0),
        atoms=[at("La", "La", 0.0505, 0.25, 0.9945, 0.5), at("Mn", "Mn", 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.4),
               at("O1", "O", 0.4876, 0.25, 0.0804, 0.6), at("O2", "O", 0.2837, 0.0368, 0.7155, 0.6)])
def neutron(): return rx.Instrument.constant_wavelength_neutron(2.4, fwhm_deg=0.5)
grid = np.arange(10.0, 150.0, 0.1)
truth = rx.Refinement(rx.Structure(phases=[phase()]), neutron())
y = np.asarray(truth.predict(grid)) + 300.0 + 2.0 * grid
y = np.maximum(y + np.random.default_rng(1).normal(scale=np.sqrt(np.maximum(y, 1.0))), 0)
data = rx.PatternData(two_theta=grid.tolist(), intensity=y.tolist())

def fresh():
    ins = neutron(); ins.background = rx.auto_background(data, two_theta_limits=(10.0, 150.0))
    for c in ins.background.coefficients: c.value = float(np.percentile(y, 10))    # the skill's seeding rule
    return rx.Refinement(rx.Structure(phases=[phase()]), ins)

bkg = ["instrument.background.*"]
print("Rietveld from the true structure, background free:",
      round(fresh().fit(data, plan=rx.RefinementPlan(stages=[rx.Stage("bkg", bkg)])).statistics.rwp, 4))
for cycles in (3, 100, 400):
    r = fresh().fit(data, mode="lebail", plan=rx.RefinementPlan(stages=[rx.Stage("bkg", bkg, lebail_cycles=cycles)]))
    print(f"Le Bail, cell and profile at the truth, background free, lebail_cycles={cycles}:", round(r.statistics.rwp, 4))
r = fresh().fit(data, mode="pawley", plan=rx.RefinementPlan(stages=[rx.Stage("bkg", bkg), rx.Stage("int", ["phases.*.reflections.*"])]))
print("Pawley, the same:", round(r.statistics.rwp, 4))
```

</details>

## Impact

A benchmark of a CW-neutron Le Bail → Rietveld workflow found Le Bail Rwp above the Rietveld Rwp of the same pattern ; the result above shows it from synthetic data. It matters wherever the Le Bail Rwp is read as the best this cell and profile can do (the `lebail_gap` ratio, the skill's stop rule).

## Not settled

Whether this is the EM partition itself (the updates saturate while many reflections overlap, which is when high angle is dense) or the weights it uses. Pawley is the control that says the model is able. I have not read a Le Bail implementation; the question is for the maintainer who wrote `lebail_update`.

rietx commit: `65a78ab7`.

*Authored with Claude Code on behalf of @mustachefeeling.*

comments.body:
Thanks for the clear reproducer. I ran it unchanged on `main` at 5d1f5f67.

The numbers match to the digit: Rietveld 1.09 %, Le Bail 1.63 % at 100 cycles and 1.62 % at 400, Pawley 1.06 %.

I then asked whether the EM partition or the background is responsible. The background looks responsible. After your single Le Bail stage the fitted background is 0.88 of the true one at 100 degrees and 0.95 at 140 degrees. The residual rms is 1.85, 2.34 and 1.74 in the three bands from 90 degrees up. Running the same stage twice, so the second partitions on the background the first fitted, gives 1.18 %. Three stages give 1.10 %, with every band between 0.94 and 1.16. A single stage seeded at the Rietveld fit's own background gives 1.09 %.

So the partition reaches the Pawley level when it starts from a background that is right. More cycles do not help, because the partition settles to a fixed point that depends on the background it is given. I have not isolated why the deficit shows at high angle. My reading is that dense reflections absorb the seed's shortfall there. I did not test your second observation, that the pass-by-pass Rwp rises in a `profile_only` run.

This is a second case of the failure in `docs/wp/1542-a-le-bail-background-left-at-its-seed.md`, so I have placed it there. Your numbers go into that work package as evidence for its protocol task, and its low-seed finding now has a case where Rwp rises as well as falls.

*Reviewed with Claude Code on behalf of @yue-here.*
